title: What If Fusion Power Worked? It Did Once, With a Catch

scenes.text: What if fusion power worked? It did once. There's a catch.
On December 5, 2022, the National Ignition Facility fired its giant lasers at a tiny fuel capsule.
The lasers delivered 2.05 megajoules to the target.
The fusion burst released 3.15 megajoules, the first time a lab got more fusion energy out than the laser energy delivered to the target.
The catch: those lasers drew about 300 megajoules from the power grid to make that pulse.
So it was a scientific win, not a power plant. A real plant needs far more gain, and many shots every second.

description:
What if fusion power worked? In December 2022 a US lab got more fusion energy out than the laser energy it put on the target.
But the lasers themselves drew about 300 megajoules from the grid.
What should we run through next?
